Press Release10 November 2026Siemens AGMunich

Siemens to expand portfolio for semiconductor design and verification with the planned acquisition of Lauterbach

  • Planned acquisition will enable Siemens to integrate hardware-assisted verification with embedded software debug and trace technology into a single workflow
  • Combined workflow to empower customers to identify hardware and software issues earlier, boost engineering productivity, and accelerate time-to-market
Siemens has signed an agreement to acquire Lauterbach, a leading provider of debug and trace solutions for embedded software and complex system-on-chip (SoC) architectures. Lauterbach develops comprehensive, modular and extensible development and verification tools for microprocessors and embedded CPU cores in the form of hardware-assisted debuggers and real-time trace tools. The combination of Siemens’ and Lauterbach’s complementary technologies enables a unified view of chip and software behavior and helps customers more quickly identify errors arising from complex interactions between hardware and software during chip development. The results are faster time to revenue and higher product quality.
  • Planned acquisition will enable Siemens to integrate hardware-assisted verification with embedded software debug and trace technology into a single workflow
  • Combined workflow to empower customers to identify hardware and software issues earlier, boost engineering productivity, and accelerate time-to-market
Siemens has signed an agreement to acquire Lauterbach, a leading provider of debug and trace solutions for embedded software and complex system-on-chip (SoC) architectures. Lauterbach develops comprehensive, modular and extensible development and verification tools for microprocessors and embedded CPU cores in the form of hardware-assisted debuggers and real-time trace tools. The combination of Siemens’ and Lauterbach’s complementary technologies enables a unified view of chip and software behavior and helps customers more quickly identify errors arising from complex interactions between hardware and software during chip development. The results are faster time to revenue and higher product quality.

Siemens has signed an agreement to acquire Lauterbach, a leading provider of debug and trace solutions for embedded software and complex system-on-chip (SoC) architectures

The planned acquisition represents another important step in further establishing Siemens’ position as one of the world's leading electronic design automation (EDA) powerhouses. By adding industry-leading debugging technologies to its hardware-assisted verification solutions, Siemens is further extending its competitive edge. The planned combined solution will enable customers to develop and verify embedded software even earlier, and well before the physical chip is available.
By bringing together these previously separate workflows into a single solution Siemens aims to empower customers with a unified hardware/software view of how increasingly complex application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) and system-on-a-chip (SoC) devices behave. This shift-left approach helps customers analyze hardware/software interactions at an early stage and significantly shortens the time-to-market for new software-defined products.
“With Lauterbach, we are further extending our industry-leading EDA portfolio for semiconductor design by bringing together our premier hardware-assisted verification portfolio with its industry-leading software debugging technologies. As semiconductors represent a core vertical for our technology strategy, this enables customers to test and optimize their products even before the actual chip is produced – significantly reducing development time,” said Cedrik Neike, Member of the Managing Board of Siemens AG and President Digital Industries.
“Lauterbach is a remarkable success story, written in Germany for the global semiconductor industry. We will build on the impressive legacy that founders Lothar and Stephan Lauterbach and their team have achieved over the past decades and are very pleased to welcome the Lauterbach group to Siemens. We are also delighted that Stephan Lauterbach and Thomas Ullmann will continue their work as part of Siemens following the closing of the transaction.”
Lauterbach and Siemens solutions are already used by numerous mutual customers. The increasing complexity of modern semiconductors and embedded software, driven by trends such as artificial intelligence, software-defined vehicles, Internet of Things (IoT), multi-core architectures, cybersecurity and functional safety, is leading to greater convergence between hardware and software development. On that basis, Siemens expects significant revenue synergies from the transaction.
Headquartered close to Munich, Germany, Lauterbach was co-founded by the brothers Lothar and Stephan Lauterbach beginning in 1979 to develop tools for microprocessor development in the form of hardware-assisted debuggers and real-time trace tools. Lauterbach employs around 170 people and serves more than 1,200 global customers across various industries, including leaders and innovators in automotive, semiconductors and telecommunications. In 2025, the company generated roughly € 60 million in revenues.
“The increasing convergence of hardware and software development is fundamentally changing the industry and our customers’ requirements,” said Stephan Lauterbach, CTO and co-founder of Lauterbach. “By combining our debug and trace technology with Siemens’ hardware-assisted verification capabilities, we are creating a powerful solution that provides developers with a unified hardware/software view of the behavior of increasingly complex ASIC and SoC devices in AI, high-performance computing, storage/hyperscale, automotive, communications and A&D applications. Our commitment to keeping our customers at the center of everything we do remains unchanged.”
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and required regulatory approvals.

Lauterbach is a leading manufacturer of cutting-edge development tools for embedded systems, with more than 45 years of experience. It is an international, well-established company that serves customers all over the world, partners with all major semiconductor manufacturers and continues to grow steadily. At its headquarters in Hoehenkirchen near Munich, the engineering team develops and produces highly capable, specialized and easy-to-use development tools under the TRACE32® brand. Branch offices in the United Kingdom, Italy, France, Tunisia, on the East and West Coast of the United States, Japan and China, along with highly qualified sales and support engineers in many other countries, make Lauterbach’s full product range available worldwide. Press Release06 November 2026Siemens MobilityMunich

Siemens opens new state-of-the-art rail infrastructure technology and innovation center in Chippenham

  • UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and UK Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander official open rail infrastructure facility
  • €115 million investment to secure 800 local jobs and support the future of digital rail technology in the United Kingdom
  • World-class innovation hub exports 40% of products globally and will design, test and build digital signaling technology
  • Highly sustainable facility designed to meet the highest environmental standards, reinforcing Siemens’ commitment to Net Zero
Siemens has officially opened its new, state-of-the-art manufacturing and research facility in Chippenham, marking a €115 million investment in the UK’s rail infrastructure. The opening was attended by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander. The new site at SouthPoint Business Park serves as a global center of excellence for signaling and control systems, replacing the historic neighboring facility. The transition to the new facility, including the transfer of all 800 local staff, was completed without any interruption in production. This milestone highlights the critical role of advanced digital technology in creating a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable railway.

  • World-class innovation hub exports 40% of products globally and will design, test and build digital signaling technology

Siemens has officially opened its new, state-of-the-art manufacturing and research facility in Chippenham, marking a €115 million investment in the UK’s rail infrastructure. The opening was attended by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander. The new site at SouthPoint Business Park serves as a global center of excellence for signaling and control systems, replacing the historic neighboring facility. The transition to the new facility, including the transfer of all 800 local staff, was completed without any interruption in production. This milestone highlights the critical role of advanced digital technology in creating a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable railway.

From right to left: The opening was attended by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander. Photo source: Siemens Mobility

“Siemens Mobility's new rail technology centre is a real boost for Chippenham and a vote of confidence in Britain's rail industry. The digital signaling produced on site will help our railways become more reliable and safer, whilst strengthening our skills base by supporting hundreds of local jobs and apprenticeships” commented Heidi Alexander, UK Secretary of State for Transport.
„Our new Chippenham factory and innovation center is a testament to our deep roots and long-term commitment to the UK, and our belief in the talented workforce and innovation found here. For over a century, this town has been a powerhouse of rail engineering. With our €115 million investment, we are ensuring that Chippenham will lead the digital rail revolution into the future for decades to come. We are proud to provide the technology that transforms the everyday for millions of rail passengers, both here in the United Kingdom and worldwide,” said Michael Peter, President of Siemens Mobility.
The new Siemens facility marks the next chapter for a historic rail hub that dates back to 1897. Originally established by Evans O’Donnell and later the headquarters of the Westinghouse Brake & Signaling Company, Chippenham has been a global center of excellence for over a century, delivering critical technology for iconic projects like London’s Elizabeth, Victoria, and Central lines. This legacy of innovation is now being carried forward into a world-class, sustainable environment at SouthPoint Business Park. Built to the BREEAM 'Excellent' standard, the new site features energy-efficient offices and production areas designed to blend with their surroundings, including a 10% net increase in biodiversity through native planting. This modern, collaborative workspace enables Siemens to scale the production of advanced systems, such as computer-based interlockings and the European Train Control System (ETCS), ensuring that Chippenham remains at the heart of the UK’s digital rail revolution.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham (pictured) and UK Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander official open rail infrastructure facility. Photo source: Siemens Mobility DE: Britischer Premierminister Andy Burnham (im Foto) und die britische Verkehrsministerin Heidi Alexander eröffnen offiziell den neuen Standort für Bahninfrastruktur. Fotoquelle: Siemens Mobility

Primary-age children get the first look at the new rail factory
To celebrate the opening of the new facility, Siemens hosted a hands-on STEM lesson for local pupils, which was broadcast to more than 1,000 children nationwide. The session was delivered by British award-winning children’s presenter Maddie Moate.
The event reflects a growing national focus on employers introducing children to the world of work from primary school age onwards. Last year, Siemens UK&I welcomed 326 apprentices, graduates, and interns into the business, and through the National Training Academy for Rail, has trained more than 28,000 people
Last year, our education and skills activities reached more than 600,000 students, teachers and members of the community and supported over 2,800 schools across the country. Almost 13,000 people also took part in our virtual work experience offer, helping us reach young people from a much broader range of backgrounds.
Siemens Mobility in the United Kingdom
Siemens is a cornerstone of the UK’s transport sector, employing approximately 5,000 people nationwide. The opening of the new Chippenham factory and innovation center is part of a wider investment strategy in the United Kingdom, which includes the new €230 million rail village in Goole and a comprehensive network of maintenance depots. By combining over a century of local heritage with world-class digital innovation, Siemens Mobility remains a key partner in driving the UK’s industrial strategy and shaping a smarter, more sustainable future for the country’s infrastructure.

Press Release05 November 2026Siemens MobilityMunich

Siemens to supply Taiwan’s Taoyuan Metro with Signaling X technology

  • Siemens brings its latest Signaling X technology to Taiwan
  • Contract includes equipping two metro lines in Taoyuan with latest signaling technology and GoA4 automation
  • Commissioning of the new sections is scheduled for the mid-2030s
  • Siemens brings its latest Signaling X technology to Taiwan
  • Contract includes equipping two metro lines in Taoyuan with latest signaling technology and GoA4 automation
  • Commissioning of the new sections is scheduled for the mid-2030s

From left to right: Siemens Mobility GmbH Taiwan Branch’s Finance Director, Ms. Georgia Shih, with former Managing Director, Mr. Thomas Stein, and Mr. Gareth Tang, President, Urban Solutions, ST Engineering and Mr. Koh Chan Tia, Head, Global Sales, Urban Solutions, ST Engineering signed new contracts to deliver Signaling X solutions for Taoyuan’s Brown Line and Green Line Extension.

Siemens has been awarded the signaling contracts for two major Taoyuan metro projects by ST Engineering’s Urban Solutions business, the turnkey rail services provider leading project management and systems integration, at this year’s Singapore Urban Mobility Week. Siemens is bringing its latest Signaling X technology to Taiwan, setting new standards for the future of rail signaling. Siemens will deliver the approximately 11-kilometer Taoyuan Brown Line – including eight stations (both underground and elevated) – as well as the Taoyuan Green Line Extension, which connects the Green Line towards Zhongli (A23) and establishes vital future connectivity to the major multi-level transit hub. The projects will leverage advanced digital signaling technologies, including GoA4 fully automated train operation and ATS (Automatic Train Supervision). 
"We are proud to bring our latest Signaling X technology to Taiwan," said Marc Ludwig, Executive Vice President Rail Infrastructure at Siemens Mobility. "This marks a major milestone in the digitalization of rail transport as we deploy our new generation of software-defined signaling technology for the Taoyuan Metro. Together with ST Engineering, we are building on our existing experience in Taoyuan to reduce interface complexity and support efficient project delivery, while providing the foundation for safe, reliable and fully automated operations."
The project exemplifies the shift from hardware-centric signaling systems to a software-defined, virtualized architecture, allowing existing infrastructure to be modernized more easily, flexibly and efficiently. Signaling X connects proven rail technologies with a new generation of digital capabilities, driving the digital transformation of rail infrastructure. 
Signaling X as the technology foundation for next-generation rail signaling
Signaling X is Siemens’ integrated technology foundation for the digital transformation of rail infrastructure. It brings together safety-critical and non-safety-critical applications, open interfaces and services. The core of the architecture lies in the decoupling of software from proprietary hardware, allowing applications to run on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware instead of dedicated proprietary components. This paradigm shift allows operators to modernize and scale their infrastructure independently of specific hardware lifecycles. Maintenance is simplified, and spare parts management becomes more efficient by leveraging globally available IT standards. The DS3 (Distributed Smart Safe System) safety platform provides a redundant environment with highest possible availability, in which safety-critical applications meet the highest requirements according to CENELEC Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL4). Signaling X follows secure-by-design and zero-trust principles for the operation of critical infrastructure.
